section_summary: This section contains successive secret Joint Army–Air weekly intelligence summaries sent from Tokyo between October and December 1949, each generally preceded by a State Department incoming-telegram cover sheet. They report Japanese politics, economic conditions and repatriation; North Korean force expansion; Philippine elections and unrest; political developments in Okinawa; and aircraft movements in the western Pacific. The section begins and ends within weekly reports whose other pages lie outside the supplied text.

subfiles.title: Joint WEEKA 55, concluding pages
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Far East, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The concluding pages report North Korean propaganda, Philippine election tensions and Huk activity, Okinawan politics, and Chinese Nationalist aircraft deliveries.
subfiles.summary: The report describes North Korea's rejection of UN activity, escalating Philippine election pressure and police concerns, arms smuggling, and Huk attacks on aircraft. It also notes a People's Party membership drive in Okinawa and a B-25 delivery route through Guam.

subfiles.title: State Department incoming-telegram cover for Joint WEEKA 56
subfiles.about: The cover records receipt and routing of Joint WEEKA 56.
subfiles.summary: Routes the October 28 Army message from Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Joint WEEKA 56
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Far East, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for CSGID
subfiles.about: The report surveys Japan, North Korean forces, the Philippine election and Huk movement, and Okinawan politics.
subfiles.summary: Japan closes schools run by the League of Koreans and resumes Diet business. The report assesses North Korean border forces, tanks, and Korean troops entering from Manchuria. It examines Philippine candidates, possible election violence, relations with Communist China, and Huk operations. In Okinawa it reports a replacement assembly and left-wing People's Party activity.

subfiles.title: State Department incoming-telegram cover for Joint WEEKA 57
subfiles.about: The cover records receipt and routing of Joint WEEKA 57.
subfiles.summary: Routes the November 4 Army message from Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Joint WEEKA 57
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Far East, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for CSGID
subfiles.about: The report covers Japanese politics and repatriates, North Korean troop reports, Philippine election violence, and Ryukyu and Guam affairs.
subfiles.summary: It describes Japanese political disputes and Soviet-directed attempts to influence returning prisoners. It evaluates reports of North Korean and Chinese Communist forces, then warns of intimidation and bloodshed around the Philippine election. It also records allegations of uranium deposits, Okinawan administrative disputes and electricity shortages, and Guam labor and immigration concerns.

subfiles.title: State Department incoming-telegram cover for Joint WEEKA 58

subfiles.summary: Routes the November 12 Army message from Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Joint WEEKA 58
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Far East, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for CSGID
subfiles.about: The report covers Yoshida's peace-treaty speech, North Korean military buildup, the Philippine election, and Okinawan officials' arrests.
subfiles.summary: It summarizes Yoshida's Diet speech and reactions, Japanese economic and repatriation developments, and reports of North Korean tanks and Chinese Communist troops. Philippine coverage concerns election security, possible retaliation, a Communist Party court petition, and farm mechanization. The report also records the jailing of Naha's mayor and vice mayor and alleged Ryukyu currency counterfeiting.

subfiles.title: State Department incoming-telegram cover for Joint WEEKA 59
subfiles.about: The cover records receipt and routing of Joint WEEKA 59.
subfiles.summary: Routes the November 18 Army message from Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Joint WEEKA 59
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Far East, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for CSGID
subfiles.about: The report discusses Japanese peace-treaty politics, North Korean force organization, alleged Philippine election fraud, and Ryukyu developments.
subfiles.summary: Following the death of Upper House president Matsudaira, Japanese debate over a peace treaty intensifies. The report assesses North Korean border and army units, and extensive allegations of Philippine election fraud and possible armed opposition. It also covers Philippine plans for a Southeast Asia union, Indonesian trade, the Naha mayoral race, and Guam labor complaints.

subfiles.title: State Department incoming-telegram cover for Joint WEEKA 60
subfiles.about: The cover records receipt and routing of Joint WEEKA 60.
subfiles.summary: Routes the November 25 Army message from Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Joint WEEKA 60
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Far East, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for CSGID
subfiles.about: The report covers Japanese party disputes, Korean troop movements, Philippine post-election politics, and Okinawan elections and smuggling.
subfiles.summary: It tracks a split among coalition Democrats in Japan and continued repatriation demands. Reports from North Korea concern Chinese Communist Korean troops, military assistance, and surveillance. Philippine items include indemnity demands for a Japanese treaty, Nacionalista fraud claims, economic concerns, and Huk incidents. Okinawan coverage concerns mayoral elections and smuggling; Guam reports further B-25 deliveries.

subfiles.title: Joint WEEKA 61
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Far East, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for CSGID
subfiles.about: The report assesses Japanese political and economic issues, North Korean Chinese Communist troops and naval forces, and Philippine and Ryukyu developments.
subfiles.summary: Japanese coverage includes a widening Democratic Party split and repatriation. The report weighs conflicting figures for Korean troops entering North Korea from Manchuria and describes reported naval commands. Philippine coverage includes the Nacionalistas' legal response to Quirino's victory, import controls, and dissident attacks. It records Okinawan mayoral results and a submarine sighting near Saipan.

subfiles.title: Joint WEEKA 62
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Far East, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for CSGID
subfiles.about: The report follows Japanese food controls, North Korean troop movements, Philippine policy and insurgency, and Pacific air activity.
subfiles.summary: Japan's food procurement bill meets opposition while repatriates continue protests. The report examines uncertain estimates of Chinese Communist troops in North Korea. It covers Quirino's regional diplomacy, investment and import rules, a Moro insurrection in Sulu, and Huk movements. Air sections discuss interference at Itazuke, Philippine fighter shortages, and another B-25 routed through Guam.

subfiles.title: State Department incoming-telegram cover for Joint WEEKA 63

subfiles.title: Joint WEEKA 63
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Far East, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for CSGID
subfiles.about: The report covers Japanese food and labor disputes, Korean troop estimates, Philippine political reconciliation and rebellion, and Chinese Nationalist aircraft on Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: It reports Japan's food procurement ordinance, railway wage dispute, anti-Communist labor congress, and recent repatriates. North Korean sections scrutinize a large estimate of Korean troops from Chinese Communist forces and describe divisions near the 38th parallel. Philippine sections cover a Quirino–Avelino agreement, Batangas and Sulu fighting, and an alleged uranium deposit. The closing air report compares observed Chinese Nationalist aircraft on Taiwan with existing intelligence estimates.

subfiles.title: Joint WEEKA 64, opening pages
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Far East, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Department of the Army for CSGID
subfiles.about: The opening pages report Japanese year-end politics and economic conditions, repatriation demands, and North Korea's Seventh Border Constabulary Brigade.
subfiles.summary: The report lists disputed Japanese year-end allowances, budget plans, currency and crop figures, and a request for Soviet statistics on missing Japanese prisoners. It then assesses claims that Chinese Communist Korean personnel joined North Korea's Seventh Border Constabulary Brigade. The report continues beyond page 423.
